public_rationale: WIRED contemporaneously reported that Gemini generated a historically incorrect Apollo 11 crew image. This supports the ordinary contextual complaint that Gemini got the crew wrong. The evidence concerns image generation; it does not establish a universal inability to identify the astronauts or a failure of textual recall.
limitations: Relies on reputable news reporting because an authenticated original interaction was not obtained.
The result depends on accepting an incorrect crew depiction as the failure Marcus described.
The report does not provide a failure rate.

statement.excerpt: So let me get this straight? Sora’s can’t reliably handle basic physics, ChatGPT had an unexplained meltdown, Gemini can’t even remember who was on Apollo 11, there are no formal guarantees that any of this will ever work, you yourself admit you don’t know how it works, or how much better it will get next time around, and you want another $7 trillion dollars?
statement.document_title: Belief in magic may be declining

our_interpretation: Read as a complaint about a documented erroneous Apollo 11 crew response, rather than a claim that every possible prompt fails.
A historically incorrect depiction of the crew counts as an erroneous response, although it does not establish inability to name the astronauts in text.
The post gives no exact incident date. Use February 2024 through publication as the contemporaneous reporting period.
criteria.support_condition: A reliable contemporaneous record shows Gemini incorrectly identifying or depicting the Apollo 11 crew.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The alleged crew error is shown to be fabricated, misattributed, or a correct response to a materially different prompt. One successful response would not disprove an observed failure.
